title: S3 Presigned URLs
description: Generate secure, time-limited upload and download URLs for client-side S3 access.

data.text: Presigned URLs let your ASP.NET Core app grant temporary S3 access to clients without exposing AWS credentials. They are commonly used for direct browser uploads and downloads.

data.title: Create a presigned PUT URL

data.text: The client can use the presigned URL with a simple HTTP PUT request, including the file bytes and Content-Type header.

data.title: Upload with HttpClient
data.content: Use `HttpClient` to PUT the file to the presigned URL.

data.text: For downloads, use `HttpVerb.GET` and set the response content disposition if you want the browser to prompt for a filename.

data.title: Build a presigned URL API
data.description: Create endpoints that return presigned URLs for upload and download.
steps: Generate a PUT presigned URL valid for 10 minutes
Generate a GET presigned URL with a Content-Disposition header
Test both URLs from a browser or curl
data.expectedOutcome: Clients can upload and download files directly from S3 using presigned URLs.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Presigned URLs delegate temporary S3 access without sharing credentials
Use PUT for uploads and GET for downloads
Set short expiration times for security
Presigned URLs work with any HTTP client
data.takeaway: Presigned URLs are the standard pattern for direct client-to-S3 uploads in ASP.NET Core.
